subtype: Approach: copy an influencer's routine and diet [Pitfall]
passage:
Kamal watched a video reel of a man who ate almost nothing and lifted enormous weights, and decided to copy him from Monday. It was exam season, his college was an hour away by bus, and he had never lifted anything heavier than a bag. He didn't care.

The first week, he skipped two meals and made himself lift until his arms shook. By Thursday every step felt like torture, and hunger made him snap at his cousin Pranav over nothing.

"That man has a different body, a different day and probably a coach," Pranav said. "You have a viva on Friday." Kamal ignored him. Ten days later, sore and starving, he quit everything and told nobody why.

qa.q: How far was Kamal's college by bus?
What was Kamal feeling when he snapped at Pranav?
qa.a: Kamal was hungry, sore and irritable, and pushing hard to prove he could follow the plan.

qa.q: What could Kamal do instead of copying the reel, and why?
qa.a: Kamal could build a plan around his own timetable and start light, because a routine that fits his body and schedule is more likely to last.

qa.q: How does Pranav see Kamal's plan?
qa.a: Pranav sees a plan borrowed from someone with a different body and different demands, and is worried about Kamal during exams.

grounding: The person follows a reel plan of extreme cuts and heavy lifts without regard to body or schedule, and quits within two weeks.

subtype: Approach: copy an influencer's routine and diet [Pitfall]
passage:
Yash found the plan on a fitness reel on a Sunday night in his Pune flat: heavy lifting six days a week and a diet of mostly boiled eggs and shakes, with meals cut to almost nothing. The man in the video had a six-pack and said, "No days off."
Yash copied it into his notes. He didn't ask anyone, not even his flatmate Imran, who went to a gym and had once hurt his shoulder.
By Wednesday he could barely lift his arms to comb his hair. By the next week he was so hungry during meetings he couldn't concentrate, and he snapped at an intern. His back ached from the heavy lifts he'd never tried before.
On day eleven he skipped the gym, ate three plates of rajma chawal, and deleted the note. "It doesn't work for me," he told Imran.
"It wasn't made for you," Imran said.

qa.q: What did Yash eat on day eleven?
qa.a: He ate three plates of rajma chawal.

qa.q: How did Yash feel during the second week, and what shows it?
qa.a: He felt exhausted, sore and irritable, too hungry to concentrate in meetings and snapping at an intern.

qa.q: What approach would have suited Yash better than copying the reel?
qa.a: He could have started with a routine built around his own body and schedule, perhaps with Imran's help or a trainer, and kept eating normal meals.

qa.q: How does Imran see Yash's attempt?
qa.a: Imran sees it clearly as someone else's routine that was never made for Yash, and may feel sorry he wasn't asked earlier.

grounding: Shows a person copying a reel's extreme diet and heavy-lifting plan without regard to body or schedule and quitting within two weeks.

subtype: Approach: copy an influencer's routine and diet [Pitfall]
passage:
"Why are you walking like a robot?" Pranav asked as Vaibhav came into the hostel room.
"Leg day. Day four of the plan."
"Which plan?"
"That fitness guy's. Lifting every day, and I've cut my meals right down like he does." Vaibhav lowered himself onto the bed very slowly.
"You haven't lifted anything heavier than your laptop since school."
"He says the pain means it's working."
"And the food?"
"I skipped dinner. I'm fine."
A week later Pranav found him in the mess with two plates of poha.
"The plan?"
Vaibhav didn't look up. "I quit. I was starving in every lecture, fell asleep in the lab, and my knees hurt on the stairs." He sighed. "He's probably been training for ten years. I did it for nine days."
"Maybe start with something that fits you?"
"Maybe. I'm just done for now."

qa.q: How many days did Vaibhav follow the plan?
qa.a: He followed it for nine days.

qa.q: How does Vaibhav seem to feel when he says he quit?
qa.a: He seems discouraged and embarrassed, not looking up from his plates and saying he is just done for now.

qa.q: What would you advise Vaibhav to try next?
qa.a: Start with a small routine that fits his own body and timetable, and keep eating proper meals, instead of copying someone who has trained for years.

qa.q: How might Pranav feel watching Vaibhav's week?
qa.a: Pranav seems amused at first but also worried, and gently suggests something that fits Vaibhav better.

grounding: Shows a person copying an influencer's routine of extreme food cuts and heavy lifts and quitting within two weeks because it did not fit.
